title: Aurora UI vs Liquid Glass
lede: Both are dark pages with colour bleeding through translucent panels. One animates the light source; the other treats the panel as the material.
verdict: Aurora moves the background: soft colour fields drift behind static glass. Liquid Glass holds the background still and puts the work into the panel edge — a hard inset highlight and a heavier border, with no shadow at all.
brief: Aurora UI is a background technique. The panels barely change — a 1px border at 14 to 18 percent white and a modest blur — while the colour behind them drifts on 14 to 22 second cycles. Switch the animation off and the page still reads as aurora, because the colour field is the identity.

Liquid Glass is a surface technique. The field behind is two strong radial gradients pinned to the viewport, and it does not move. All the character is in the card: a 28 percent border, a 1px inset highlight at 55 percent along the top edge, and deliberately no drop shadow, so the panel reads as a slab rather than a floating pane.

dimensions.name: Panel edge
dimensions.b: 1px at 28% plus an inset top highlight

dimensions.b: #0b1020 with two fixed radials at 50% scrim

dimensions.name: Failure mode
dimensions.b: A flat field leaves the highlight with nothing to catch

cssDelta.label: Background motion
cssDelta.a: three fields on 16s to 22s alternate loops

whenA: The page is a hero or a landing section where atmosphere is the point and reading is brief
You want the site to feel alive without any interaction
The content sits in one short block rather than a long scroll
whenB: Panels are the interface — cards, modals, sidebars — and each needs a clear edge
You want the look without any animation, which makes it far easier to keep accessible
The background is a photograph or a video rather than a gradient field
promptDelta: Ask for drifting radial gradients and you get Aurora; ask for an inset top highlight, a 28 percent border and no shadow and you get Liquid Glass. The two are often generated together by accident — a model asked for glassmorphism with a fancy background will produce both, and the result is a moving field under panels that also have drop shadows, which is three depth cues fighting. Pick one: motion behind static glass, or a static field with material panels.
